pathway.title: NCL CORP Ltd. — Credit Snapshot
pathway.question: Should we own this issuer, in which instrument, and why?

runs.text: First, leverage is high and has risen. NCLC carried balance-sheet debt of USD 14,884.5 million at September 30, 2026 against last-twelve-months Adjusted EBITDA of USD 2,700.1 million, which is 5.51x, and 5.42x net of USD 250.7 million of cash; at FY2025 the figures were 5.34x and 5.26x on USD 2,731.4 million of Adjusted EBITDA [CP-1]. Adjusted EBITDA for Q3 2026 was USD 936.7 million against USD 1,019.4 million, with Net Yield per Capacity Day at USD 319.65 against USD 341.89, so volume is growing while price per unit falls [CP-1; Q3 10-Q page:34]. The parent states net leverage of 5.5x on its own perimeter; that is a consistent but separate measure and is not used here (Documentary Fact and Analyst Interpretation).

Second, near-term liquidity is adequate on the issuer's own filings. At September 30, 2026 NCLC had cash of USD 250.7 million and revolver availability of about USD 1,100 million, which the filing totals as liquidity of about USD 1.4 billion [Q3 10-Q page:6]. Scheduled principal is USD 238.6 million for the rest of 2026 and USD 1,105.7 million in 2027 [CP-1]. In October 2026 NCLC issued USD 950.0 million of 8.750% senior unsecured notes due 2031, repaid USD 380.0 million of revolver borrowings, redeemed the 6.125% notes due 2028 and raised revolver commitments from about USD 2.5 billion to about USD 2.8 billion, which on printed figures lifts revolver availability to about USD 1,780 million (calculated); the parent's own pro forma figure is USD 1.8 billion and is parent-level [Q3 10-Q page:12; Q3 release page:3].

Third, the revolver carries a springing maturity that falls 12 days after the as-of date. The 10-K states that if on November 17, 2026 the 2027 1.125% or 2.5% exchangeable notes have not been repaid or refinanced with debt maturing after April 23, 2030 and a liquidity test is not satisfied, the commitments and loans mature on November 17, 2026 [10-K page:142]. Both series mature on February 15, 2027 and total USD 216.2 million of principal; NCLC states it expects to repay them in cash or refinance before maturity, and held USD 250.7 million of cash [Q3 10-Q page:38]. The liquidity test is not defined in the pages read, the Q3 10-Q does not restate the clause, and the October 2026 third amendment may have changed it. This is a missing datapoint, not an adverse finding, but it is the most time-sensitive item because the facility is the main liquidity backstop (Insufficient Information).

Fourth, capital commitments are large, mostly financed and partly open. Non-cancelable ship contracts total USD 19,421.2 million for 13 effective ships, with committed undrawn export-credit facilities of about USD 10.8 billion funding about 80% of most contracts; three effective contracts (Oceania Sonata Class 3 in 2032, Regent Prestige Class 3 in 2033 and Oceania Sonata Class 4 in 2035) are “Contract effective, but not yet financed” [Q3 10-Q page:20, page:41 and page:42]. Anticipated ship construction and growth spending is USD 1.1 billion for the rest of 2026, USD 3.1 billion in 2027 and USD 1.8 billion in 2028, against export-credit funding of USD 0.6 billion, USD 2.0 billion and USD 1.3 billion [Q3 10-Q page:40]. The unfunded part in 2027, USD 1.1 billion, plus scheduled principal of USD 1,105.7 million is USD 2,205.7 million, which is 1.02x last-twelve-months operating cash flow of USD 2,169.0 million (calculated, from printed rounded figures). Little room is left for deleveraging from internally generated cash in 2027 (Analyst Interpretation).

Fifth, the debt stack is long-dated and mostly fixed rate, which supports debt service but concentrates maturities. At September 30, 2026, 88% of debt was fixed and 12% variable, and a one percentage point rise in SOFR would raise annual interest expense by about USD 18.2 million [Q3 10-Q page:43]. Scheduled principal is USD 1,346.1 million in 2028, USD 1,370.0 million in 2029 and USD 4,134.3 million in 2030, which together are 44.2% of the USD 15,498.0 million total, and 2030 alone is 26.7% (calculated) [CP-1]. The October 2026 actions change those buckets: if the full USD 525.0 million of 6.125% notes was outstanding, 2028 falls to about USD 821.1 million; if the revolver sits in the 2030 bucket, repaying USD 380.0 million takes 2030 to about USD 3,754.3 million; and 2031 rises to about USD 2,825.1 million with the new notes (calculated, illustrative; the USD 42.2 million of export-credit prepayment is not allocated). The 2030 maturities include the revolver (stated maturity January 22, 2030), two exchangeable series and the 6.25% senior unsecured notes [10-K page:139 and page:142]. Interest expense, net fell to USD 564.5 million for nine months 2026 from USD 782.4 million, but about USD 202.5 million of the earlier amount was extinguishment loss, so the underlying fall was 2.7% (calculated) [CP-1].

Sixth, currency exposure is large on the capital side. Euro-denominated ship payments not hedged were EUR 14.1 billion (USD 16.0 billion) and unhedged euro debt about EUR 2.1 billion (USD 2.4 billion); a 10% change in the euro would change the dollar value of the unhedged payments by USD 1.6 billion and of the unhedged debt principal by USD 237.7 million [Q3 10-Q page:44]. The payments fall due over many years, so the effect on cash is gradual, but it moves the dollar cost of commitments that the export-credit loans only partly fund (Analyst Interpretation).

Seventh, covenant headroom cannot be measured. The 10-K names a loan to value ratio below 0.70 to 1.00, free liquidity of at least USD 250 million at all times, an EBITDA to consolidated debt service ratio of at least 1.25 to 1.00 unless free liquidity is at least USD 300 million, and a net funded debt to total capitalization ratio whose level is not printed [10-K page:41]. Compliance is stated at September 30, 2026 [Q3 10-Q page:13], but no ratio values are printed. Cash alone was USD 179.2 million at March 31, 2026 and USD 212.3 million at June 30, 2026, below the USD 250 million level, so the free-liquidity definition must count undrawn revolver capacity or similar sources; the definition is not supplied (Insufficient Information and Analyst Interpretation). The October 2026 amendment “also modified certain existing financial covenant definitions and the related collateral” [Q3 10-Q page:12].

Eighth, the issuer sits under a parent and the exchangeable notes link the two. NCLH owns all NCLC shares, guarantees the exchangeable notes on a senior unsecured basis, and the notes exchange into NCLH shares with cash up to principal and cash or shares for any excess [10-K page:144; CP-1A]. NCLH passed equity proceeds to NCLC in 2025 and no distribution to the parent appears in the periods read [CP-1A]. The Havana Docks matter names NCLH as defendant, was remanded to the Eleventh Circuit in June 2026 and is “reasonably possible but not probable” with no liability recorded; whether NCLC bears it is not stated [Q3 10-Q page:22] (Insufficient Information).

cells.text: “We are a leading global cruise company, which operates the Norwegian Cruise Line, Oceania Cruises and Regent Seven Seas Cruises brands.” At September 30, 2026 the combined fleet was 33 ships with approximately 72,000 Berths.
Revenue rests on discretionary leisure travel across three price tiers.

The fleet was 34 ships with approximately 71,400 Berths at December 31, 2025; the decrease since June 30, 2026 is due to Norwegian Sky and Oceania Regatta commencing long-term charters to third parties.
Chartered-out ships leave the operated fleet and the earnings base, but may be retained as assets.
The business has a single reportable segment; each brand is a business for which discrete information is available.
No segment diversification inside the issuer.

Passenger ticket revenue (accommodation, meals, entertainment, taxes and port fees, air and land packages) and onboard and other revenue (casino, beverage, shore excursions, specialty dining, retail, spa, Wi-Fi and long-term ship charters). Nine months 2026 revenue was 5,217.8 passenger ticket and 2,700.7 onboard and other (US$m).
Onboard revenue carries direct costs and depends on guest spending on board.

“Our revenue attributable to U.S.-sourced guests has approximated 84% of total revenue over the preceding three fiscal years.” is the concentration disclosed; revenue by destination for nine months 2026 is North America 4,991.7, Europe 2,104.9, Asia-Pacific 588.2 and Other 233.7 against 4,200.7, 2,386.5, 763.6 and 232.5 for nine months 2025 (US$m).
A single source market dominates demand; Europe and Asia-Pacific revenue fell year on year while North America rose.

Norwegian prices typically include meals in certain dining facilities and many onboard activities; Oceania Cruises prices include specialty dining, Wi-Fi, laundry and gratuities; Regent fares are all-inclusive including unlimited shore excursions.
Brand positioning ranges from mass-premium to luxury; pricing is the main yield lever.
Capacity Days, occupancy and Net Yield: for Q3 2026 Net Yield per Capacity Day was 319.65 against 341.89 and occupancy 106.5% against 106.4%.
Volume grew while yield fell, so earnings depend on price recovery.
“Our operations are seasonal and results for interim periods are not necessarily indicative of the results for the entire fiscal year.” Demand is strongest in the Northern Hemisphere summer.
The third quarter carries most profit; interim leverage and liquidity swing seasonally.

Largest operating costs are payroll and related (including a third-party crew services contract), fuel, airfare, food and beverage, advertising and travel advisor services; fuel was approximately 48% hedged for the remainder of 2026.
Fuel and payroll are the volatile cost lines; hedging covers part of the fuel risk only.
Non-cancelable ship construction contracts for 13 effective newbuilds; committed undrawn export-credit facilities of approximately 10.8 billion fund approximately 80% of most contracts.
Capital spending is contractual and euro-denominated; financing is mostly committed but not complete.
“As of December 31, 2025, we had a working capital deficit of $4.4 billion” including $3.2 billion of advance ticket sales, which management describes as substantially like deferred revenue.
Customer deposits fund operations and are partly refundable, so a booking slowdown drains cash.

Approximately 5,300 full-time shoreside employees and approximately 39,200 shipboard employees at December 31, 2025; Regent and Oceania ships use a third party for additional hotel and restaurant staffing; collective bargaining agreements cover certain crew members.
Labor cost and work disruption are disclosed risks.
The company operates Great Stirrup Cay in The Bahamas and Harvest Caye in Belize; the Great Tides Waterpark at Great Stirrup Cay opened in September 2026.
Owned destinations support itineraries and onboard spend; their costs are capital items.
Primary competitors include Carnival and Royal Caribbean, as well as MSC Cruises, Viking Ocean Cruises and Virgin Voyages, and land-based vacation alternatives.
Industry capacity and pricing are set by larger peers.

runs.text: Strengths. (1) Liquidity and near-term maturities: cash of USD 250.7 million and revolver availability of about USD 1,100 million against USD 238.6 million of scheduled principal for the rest of 2026, with the revolver upsized after quarter-end (Documentary Fact; CP-1). (2) Funding model: most new ships are financed by long-dated fixed-rate export-credit loans, such as the 1.91% term loan maturing February 25, 2038 for Norwegian Luna, and about USD 10.8 billion of committed undrawn facilities remain (Documentary Fact; CP-1, Q3 10-Q page:42). (3) Fixed-rate profile: 88% of debt is fixed, so base-rate moves affect a small part of interest cost (Documentary Fact; Q3 10-Q page:43). (4) Parent support and no leakage: NCLH contributed equity proceeds in 2025 and no distributions to the parent appear in the periods read (Documentary Fact; CP-1A). (5) Operating cash flow of USD 1,709.3 million for nine months 2026 and seasonally strong third-quarter Adjusted EBITDA margin of 31.8% (Documentary Fact and calculation; CP-1). (6) Management cost and fleet actions, including run-rate savings programs and ship charters and sales, are described and under way, but are Management Language until they show in results (Management Language; CP-1A).

Weaknesses. (1) Leverage of 5.51x total and 5.42x net, higher than at FY2025 (Documentary Fact and calculation; CP-1). (2) Negative post-capex cash flow of USD 582.7 million for nine months 2026 and growth spending financed by debt (Documentary Fact and calculation; CP-1). (3) Earnings and yield softness: Q3 2026 Adjusted EBITDA down 8.1%, Net Yield lower, and a booked position that management says remains below its optimal range (Documentary Fact; CP-1, CP-1A). (4) Springing revolver maturity on November 17, 2026 with an undefined liquidity test (Insufficient Information; 10-K page:142). (5) Concentrated maturities in 2030 and an unfinanced part of the newbuild program (Documentary Fact; CP-1, Q3 10-Q page:41). (6) Currency exposure on unhedged euro payments and debt (Documentary Fact; Q3 10-Q page:44). (7) Demand concentration: about 84% of revenue from U.S.-sourced guests and customer deposits that are partly refundable (Documentary Fact; CP-1A). (8) Evidence gaps: no agreements, no covenant values, a reduced-disclosure annual report and a perimeter difference between the issuer's filings and the parent's releases (Insufficient Information; CP-0, CP-1, CP-1A).

runs.text: There is no acquisition, merger, sponsor transaction or leveraged buyout in the sources, and the context supplies no deal terms, so the transaction content is financing and fleet activity, with each item below at its stated status.

Completed in FY2025 (10-K page:141 to page:146): in January 2025 NCLC issued senior unsecured notes due 2032 and amended and restated the Revolving Loan Facility (the Seventh ARCA); in April 2025 it exchanged part of its 2025 exchangeable notes into new 2030 0.875% Exchangeable Notes; in June 2025 it amended the facility to raise commitments to approximately 2.5 billion; in September 2025 it issued 2030 0.750% Exchangeable Notes, 5.875% senior unsecured notes due 2031 and 6.250% notes due 2033 and used the exchangeable proceeds, together with the proceeds of an NCLH equity offering and cash, to repurchase most of the 2027 exchangeable notes. NCLH's equity offerings in April and September 2025 supplied cash used in those exchange and repurchase steps. Newbuild export-credit loans for Norwegian Aqua (March 2025) and Oceania Allura (July 2025) were also drawn.

Completed in 2026 (Q1 10-Q page:9; Q2 10-Q page:10; Q3 10-Q page:11 and page:32): delivery of Norwegian Luna in March 2026 with a €1.0 billion export-credit term loan at 1.91% maturing February 25, 2038; an irrevocable election in May 2026 to settle exchanges of both 2027 exchangeable note series in cash; the sale of Oceania Sirena in September 2026 with continued operation under a bareboat charter through spring 2028; the start of the Norwegian Sky bareboat charter in September 2026; and the start of a two-year time charter for Oceania Regatta in September 2026.

Executed and pending: a nine-year lease of Seven Seas Navigator executed in March 2026, commencing December 2027 (Q3 10-Q page:10); a ten-year bareboat charter for Norwegian Sun expected to commence in late 2027 (Q3 10-Q page:32); and a memorandum of agreement for the sale of Oceania Insignia, with closing in September 2027 (Q3 10-Q page:24). The sale price and the buyer are Not supplied.

New debt after the quarter and before the cutoff: on October 15, 2026 NCLC issued 950.0 of 8.750% senior unsecured notes due October 15, 2031, used with cash on hand to redeem all of the outstanding 6.125% senior notes due 2028, repay 380.0 of revolver borrowings and prepay about 42.2 of export-credit facilities, and entered into a third amendment that raised Revolving Loan Facility commitments from approximately 2.5 billion to approximately 2.8 billion and modified certain financial covenant definitions and collateral (Q3 10-Q page:11 to page:12; Q3 release page:1). The parent release adds a pro forma liquidity figure of 2.1 billion at September 30, 2026 (Q3 release page:3), which is parent-level and management-prepared. The indenture and amendment texts are Not supplied. Merger-related debt does not exist in the sources; the one liquidity effect described for the issuer is the October 2026 refinancing.

fields.value: Consistency with CP-0: this answer confirms CP-0 on each point it checked. Three refinements. First, CP-0 said the parent's release Adjusted EBITDA is "not interchangeable" with the issuer's; that holds, but the two are numerically close for Q3 2026 (the release states “of $937 million” for Q3 2026 (Q3 release, page:1) and the issuer reconciles 936,702 thousand (Q3 10-Q, page:36)), so the gap is small and the perimeter label is what matters. Second, CP-0 did not note that "2031 Notes" names two different instruments, see Debt by instrument. Third, CP-0 did not record that the 10-K carries a springing maturity on the Revolving Loan Facility tied to November 17, 2026 (a contract date after the cutoff); see Covenants and facility terms. fields.value: The reported base for the issuer, as filed, shows balance-sheet debt of 14,884.5 at Q3 2026 (current and long-term debt plus exchangeable notes at carrying value) against last-twelve-months Adjusted EBITDA of 2,700.1, which gives 5.51x, and 5.42x after deducting cash of 250.7. At FY2025 the same measures were 5.34x and 5.26x. The deterioration comes from both terms: debt carrying value rose from 14,583.4 while last-twelve-months Adjusted EBITDA slipped from 2,731.4, with the third quarter of 2026 at 936.7 against 1,019.4 a year earlier, down 8.1%. Reported net income is not a clean guide because other income of 200.1 in Q3 2026 (largely conversion-option gains) lifted net income to 631.9, above operating income of 624.2. Interest expense, net fell to 564.5 for 9M 2026 from 782.4, but the 9M 2025 figure included an extinguishment-related amount of 202.5, so the underlying fall is small. Cash interest is printed only for FY2025, so interim cash interest cover is Not supplied. Operating cash flow of 1,709.3 for 9M 2026 did not cover additions to property and equipment of 2,292.0, so growth is financed with new debt and export-credit loans; undrawn export-credit facilities of about 10.8 billion are stated against ship contracts of 19,421.2. Scheduled principal is 1,105.7 in 2027 and 4,134.3 in 2030, so the near-term profile is manageable and the 2030 wall is heavy. After the quarter, an 8.750% notes issue, a larger revolver and a covenant-definition amendment changed the picture, but only in summary form. Everything here is on the issuer's own perimeter; the parent's release shows different cash, net income, debt and leverage and is not mixed in.

fields.value: - Leverage. Evidence: Adjusted EBITDA for Q3 2026 fell 8.1% to 936.7 (Q3 10-Q page:34), while debt rose to 14,884.5. Mechanism: with a higher numerator and a lower denominator, leverage mechanically rises, and the quarter that carries most seasonal profit weakened. Implication: leverage on the issuer's own filings is 5.51x, above the 5.34x at FY2025; the company states net leverage on a parent basis of 5.5x, a consistent but non-identical measure.

fields.value: - Earnings quality. Evidence: Net Yield per Capacity Day fell to 319.65 from 341.89 in Q3 2026 and occupancy was roughly unchanged; the filing states the booked position “remains below its optimal range” (Q3 10-Q page:32). Mechanism: capacity grew (Capacity Days 6,766,454 against 6,417,724) while yield fell, so volume masks price. Implication: management describes about 125 million, 100 million and 100 million of run-rate savings as benefits to be realized over time (Q3 10-Q page:33); Adjusted Net Cruise Cost Excluding Fuel per Capacity Day was lower at 152.29 against 155.65, but the revenue side has not recovered, so earnings recovery is unproven.

Mechanism: newbuild deliveries are financed by export-credit loans at low fixed rates, such as the 1.91% Luna loan, but total debt grows with each delivery. Implication: deleveraging depends on EBITDA growth, not on free cash flow, until the newbuild cycle slows; committed ship payments of 19,421.2 stay ahead.

Evidence: availability fell to 1.1 billion at Q3 2026, then October 2026 actions raised revolver commitments from about 2.5 billion to about 2.8 billion and repaid 380.0. Mechanism: the remaining 2027 exchangeable notes (216.2 principal in total, 212.5 carrying) are classified as current at September 30, 2026, and the 2030 wall of 4,134.3 follows. Implication: near-term liquidity looks adequate on the filings, but the springing-maturity term and amended covenants need the agreements before comfort.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The credit-relevant structure is simple but concentrated. NCLC is the operating cruise subsidiary of a listed parent, owns three brands (Norwegian Cruise Line, Oceania Cruises and Regent Seven Seas Cruises) and ships them in one reportable segment, so there is no segment to diversify away from a weak brand. NCLH owns all NCLC ordinary shares, guarantees NCLC's exchangeable notes, receives NCLC's cash only subject to debt-agreement restrictions, and its equity price drives the value of the exchange option inside those notes. The operating model is a high fixed-cost, seasonal business that collects cash ahead of sailing: advance ticket sales are the main working capital funding and are partly refundable, so booking strength is the lead indicator of liquidity. Capital intensity is high and rising: the filings list 13 effective newbuild contracts, export-credit financing for roughly four fifths of most contracts, and three effective contracts that are not yet financed. In 2026 the company is actively reshaping the fleet, with long-term charters and sales of older ships, a new chief executive from February 2026, cost-saving programs and a booked position that management says remains below its optimal range. There is no sponsor, no merger and no dividend recapitalisation in the sources. The transaction content is therefore financing and fleet transactions, which are dated and described below. The sources lack governance papers for the issuer (the annual report uses a reduced disclosure format), the credit agreements, and any statement of how NCLH's strategy would be funded at NCLC. Those gaps limit, but do not block, the downstream work.

fields.value: NCL CORP Ltd. (issuer id `ncl-corp-ltd`; the filings name the registrant NCL Corporation Ltd., "NCLC"), as of 2026-11-05, pathway `credit_snapshot`, asks for the fundamental credit view from the upstream financial base and business context. Scope is NCLC and its consolidated subsidiaries in USD millions for FY2025 and the first three quarters of 2026, with no peer ranking, instrument recommendation or recovery conclusion. Execution is a host session; no provider was called.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Consistency with the handoffs: this answer confirms CP-1's figures and CP-1A's structure. It goes further in three places and corrects none. It adds the maturity dates of both 2027 exchangeable note series (February 15, 2027), which CP-1 listed only as 2027; it ties the springing revolver maturity of November 17, 2026 to those notes, which CP-1 recorded without the link; and it adds market-risk sensitivities from the Q3 10-Q that CP-1 did not use.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: NCL Corporation Ltd. is a leveraged but liquid cruise credit whose deleveraging has stalled: net debt is 5.42x last-twelve-months Adjusted EBITDA at September 30, 2026, up from 5.26x at FY2025. The strongest support is liquidity of about USD 1,350.7 million (cash of USD 250.7 million and revolver availability of about USD 1,100 million), a revolver upsized in October 2026 and, on the December 31, 2025 debt table and the 2026 events described, no senior unsecured note maturity before 2029. The weakest point is cash generation: operating cash flow less additions to property and equipment was negative USD 582.7 million for nine months 2026 while Q3 2026 Adjusted EBITDA fell 8.1%. What decides the outcome is whether 2027 yield recovers and how the November 17, 2026 springing maturity and the amended covenants resolve; neither amendment text is supplied.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: First, leverage is high and has risen. NCLC carried balance-sheet debt of USD 14,884.5 million at September 30, 2026 against last-twelve-months Adjusted EBITDA of USD 2,700.1 million, which is 5.51x, and 5.42x net of USD 250.7 million of cash; at FY2025 the figures were 5.34x and 5.26x on USD 2,731.4 million of Adjusted EBITDA [CP-1]. Adjusted EBITDA for Q3 2026 was USD 936.7 million against USD 1,019.4 million, with Net Yield per Capacity Day at USD 319.65 against USD 341.89, so volume is growing while price per unit falls [CP-1; Q3 10-Q page:34]. The parent states net leverage of 5.5x on its own perimeter; that is a consistent but separate measure and is not used here (Documentary Fact and Analyst Interpretation).

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Second, near-term liquidity is adequate on the issuer's own filings. At September 30, 2026 NCLC had cash of USD 250.7 million and revolver availability of about USD 1,100 million, which the filing totals as liquidity of about USD 1.4 billion [Q3 10-Q page:6]. Scheduled principal is USD 238.6 million for the rest of 2026 and USD 1,105.7 million in 2027 [CP-1]. In October 2026 NCLC issued USD 950.0 million of 8.750% senior unsecured notes due 2031, repaid USD 380.0 million of revolver borrowings, redeemed the 6.125% notes due 2028 and raised revolver commitments from about USD 2.5 billion to about USD 2.8 billion, which on printed figures lifts revolver availability to about USD 1,780 million (calculated); the parent's own pro forma figure is USD 1.8 billion and is parent-level [Q3 10-Q page:12; Q3 release page:3].

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Third, the revolver carries a springing maturity that falls 12 days after the as-of date. The 10-K states that if on November 17, 2026 the 2027 1.125% or 2.5% exchangeable notes have not been repaid or refinanced with debt maturing after April 23, 2030 and a liquidity test is not satisfied, the commitments and loans mature on November 17, 2026 [10-K page:142]. Both series mature on February 15, 2027 and total USD 216.2 million of principal; NCLC states it expects to repay them in cash or refinance before maturity, and held USD 250.7 million of cash [Q3 10-Q page:38]. The liquidity test is not defined in the pages read, the Q3 10-Q does not restate the clause, and the October 2026 third amendment may have changed it. This is a missing datapoint, not an adverse finding, but it is the most time-sensitive item because the facility is the main liquidity backstop (Insufficient Information).

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Fourth, capital commitments are large, mostly financed and partly open. Non-cancelable ship contracts total USD 19,421.2 million for 13 effective ships, with committed undrawn export-credit facilities of about USD 10.8 billion funding about 80% of most contracts; three effective contracts (Oceania Sonata Class 3 in 2032, Regent Prestige Class 3 in 2033 and Oceania Sonata Class 4 in 2035) are “Contract effective, but not yet financed” [Q3 10-Q page:20, page:41 and page:42]. Anticipated ship construction and growth spending is USD 1.1 billion for the rest of 2026, USD 3.1 billion in 2027 and USD 1.8 billion in 2028, against export-credit funding of USD 0.6 billion, USD 2.0 billion and USD 1.3 billion [Q3 10-Q page:40]. The unfunded part in 2027, USD 1.1 billion, plus scheduled principal of USD 1,105.7 million is USD 2,205.7 million, which is 1.02x last-twelve-months operating cash flow of USD 2,169.0 million (calculated, from printed rounded figures). Little room is left for deleveraging from internally generated cash in 2027 (Analyst Interpretation).

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Fifth, the debt stack is long-dated and mostly fixed rate, which supports debt service but concentrates maturities. At September 30, 2026, 88% of debt was fixed and 12% variable, and a one percentage point rise in SOFR would raise annual interest expense by about USD 18.2 million [Q3 10-Q page:43]. Scheduled principal is USD 1,346.1 million in 2028, USD 1,370.0 million in 2029 and USD 4,134.3 million in 2030, which together are 44.2% of the USD 15,498.0 million total, and 2030 alone is 26.7% (calculated) [CP-1]. The October 2026 actions change those buckets: if the full USD 525.0 million of 6.125% notes was outstanding, 2028 falls to about USD 821.1 million; if the revolver sits in the 2030 bucket, repaying USD 380.0 million takes 2030 to about USD 3,754.3 million; and 2031 rises to about USD 2,825.1 million with the new notes (calculated, illustrative; the USD 42.2 million of export-credit prepayment is not allocated). The 2030 maturities include the revolver (stated maturity January 22, 2030), two exchangeable series and the 6.25% senior unsecured notes [10-K page:139 and page:142]. Interest expense, net fell to USD 564.5 million for nine months 2026 from USD 782.4 million, but about USD 202.5 million of the earlier amount was extinguishment loss, so the underlying fall was 2.7% (calculated) [CP-1].

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Sixth, currency exposure is large on the capital side. Euro-denominated ship payments not hedged were EUR 14.1 billion (USD 16.0 billion) and unhedged euro debt about EUR 2.1 billion (USD 2.4 billion); a 10% change in the euro would change the dollar value of the unhedged payments by USD 1.6 billion and of the unhedged debt principal by USD 237.7 million [Q3 10-Q page:44]. The payments fall due over many years, so the effect on cash is gradual, but it moves the dollar cost of commitments that the export-credit loans only partly fund (Analyst Interpretation).

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Seventh, covenant headroom cannot be measured. The 10-K names a loan to value ratio below 0.70 to 1.00, free liquidity of at least USD 250 million at all times, an EBITDA to consolidated debt service ratio of at least 1.25 to 1.00 unless free liquidity is at least USD 300 million, and a net funded debt to total capitalization ratio whose level is not printed [10-K page:41]. Compliance is stated at September 30, 2026 [Q3 10-Q page:13], but no ratio values are printed. Cash alone was USD 179.2 million at March 31, 2026 and USD 212.3 million at June 30, 2026, below the USD 250 million level, so the free-liquidity definition must count undrawn revolver capacity or similar sources; the definition is not supplied (Insufficient Information and Analyst Interpretation). The October 2026 amendment “also modified certain existing financial covenant definitions and the related collateral” [Q3 10-Q page:12].

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Eighth, the issuer sits under a parent and the exchangeable notes link the two. NCLH owns all NCLC shares, guarantees the exchangeable notes on a senior unsecured basis, and the notes exchange into NCLH shares with cash up to principal and cash or shares for any excess [10-K page:144; CP-1A]. NCLH passed equity proceeds to NCLC in 2025 and no distribution to the parent appears in the periods read [CP-1A]. The Havana Docks matter names NCLH as defendant, was remanded to the Eleventh Circuit in June 2026 and is “reasonably possible but not probable” with no liability recorded; whether NCLC bears it is not stated [Q3 10-Q page:22] (Insufficient Information).

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Strengths. (1) Liquidity and near-term maturities: cash of USD 250.7 million and revolver availability of about USD 1,100 million against USD 238.6 million of scheduled principal for the rest of 2026, with the revolver upsized after quarter-end (Documentary Fact; CP-1). (2) Funding model: most new ships are financed by long-dated fixed-rate export-credit loans, such as the 1.91% term loan maturing February 25, 2038 for Norwegian Luna, and about USD 10.8 billion of committed undrawn facilities remain (Documentary Fact; CP-1, Q3 10-Q page:42). (3) Fixed-rate profile: 88% of debt is fixed, so base-rate moves affect a small part of interest cost (Documentary Fact; Q3 10-Q page:43). (4) Parent support and no leakage: NCLH contributed equity proceeds in 2025 and no distributions to the parent appear in the periods read (Documentary Fact; CP-1A). (5) Operating cash flow of USD 1,709.3 million for nine months 2026 and seasonally strong third-quarter Adjusted EBITDA margin of 31.8% (Documentary Fact and calculation; CP-1). (6) Management cost and fleet actions, including run-rate savings programs and ship charters and sales, are described and under way, but are Management Language until they show in results (Management Language; CP-1A).

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Weaknesses. (1) Leverage of 5.51x total and 5.42x net, higher than at FY2025 (Documentary Fact and calculation; CP-1). (2) Negative post-capex cash flow of USD 582.7 million for nine months 2026 and growth spending financed by debt (Documentary Fact and calculation; CP-1). (3) Earnings and yield softness: Q3 2026 Adjusted EBITDA down 8.1%, Net Yield lower, and a booked position that management says remains below its optimal range (Documentary Fact; CP-1, CP-1A). (4) Springing revolver maturity on November 17, 2026 with an undefined liquidity test (Insufficient Information; 10-K page:142). (5) Concentrated maturities in 2030 and an unfinanced part of the newbuild program (Documentary Fact; CP-1, Q3 10-Q page:41). (6) Currency exposure on unhedged euro payments and debt (Documentary Fact; Q3 10-Q page:44). (7) Demand concentration: about 84% of revenue from U.S.-sourced guests and customer deposits that are partly refundable (Documentary Fact; CP-1A). (8) Evidence gaps: no agreements, no covenant values, a reduced-disclosure annual report and a perimeter difference between the issuer's filings and the parent's releases (Insufficient Information; CP-0, CP-1, CP-1A).
